name: Mombasa
climate: Hot and humid all year, with sea breezes that help. The heaviest rains usually come around April to June.
food: Swahili cooking is the star here: biryani, pilau, coconut curries and street snacks like mahamri and viazi karai.
transport: Matatus and tuk-tuks get you around town, and the Likoni ferry links the island to the south coast. The SGR train connects Mombasa to Nairobi.
vibe: A relaxed, historic port city with a mix of cultures, faiths and languages. Life slows down in the afternoon heat.

name: Kwale
knownFor: Wasini Island and Kisite marine park
climate: Hot and humid on the coast, a little cooler in the Shimba Hills. Long rains usually fall from about April to June.
food: Fresh seafood, coconut rice and Swahili dishes, with plenty of tropical fruit such as mango and pineapple.
transport: Most visitors reach Diani by road from Mombasa via the Likoni ferry; there is also a small airstrip at Ukunda.
vibe: Laid-back beach life along the shore, with quiet farming villages inland.

name: Kilifi
climate: Warm to hot and humid along the coast, drier further inland. Rain is heaviest roughly from April to June.
food: Coastal Swahili food, fresh fish and seafood, and Italian restaurants in Malindi and Watamu.
transport: Buses and matatus run along the main coast road from Mombasa, and Malindi has a domestic airport.
vibe: Easy-going beach towns, creeks and historic ruins, with a creative, relaxed feel in Kilifi town.

name: Tana River
climate: Hot and mostly dry, with short rainy seasons. The river can flood after heavy rain upstream.
food: Simple local food such as rice, maize, goat meat and milk, with fish near the river.
transport: Roads are long and some are rough, so travel takes time. Public transport is limited outside the main road.
vibe: Remote and sparsely populated, built around the river and livestock. Check current travel advisories before visiting.

name: Lamu
knownFor: Lamu Old Town (UNESCO World Heritage Site)
climate: Hot and humid with steady sea breezes. The main rains usually fall from about April to June.
food: Swahili seafood, coconut dishes, samosas and strong spiced coffee sold in the streets.
transport: Most visitors fly to Manda airstrip and take a boat across. In Lamu Old Town there are almost no cars; people walk or ride donkeys.
vibe: Slow, peaceful and very traditional on the islands. Check current travel advisories for the mainland and border areas.

name: Taita-Taveta
knownFor: Tsavo East and Tsavo West National Parks
climate: Hot and dry on the plains, noticeably cooler and greener in the Taita Hills.
food: Everyday Kenyan food such as ugali, beans and greens, with bananas and vegetables from the hills.
transport: The main Nairobi–Mombasa road and the SGR pass through Voi. Safari lodges are usually reached by road or charter flight.
vibe: Big safari country with quiet hill villages; most of the county is national park.

name: Garissa
knownFor: Tana River crossing at Garissa town
climate: Very hot and dry for most of the year, with short rains around April and November.
food: Somali dishes such as camel meat, rice, anjero (a soft pancake bread) and spiced tea with camel milk.
transport: Garissa town is linked to Nairobi by a tarmac road and has an airstrip. Travel beyond the town is long and limited.
vibe: A busy trading town in the middle of wide semi-desert. Check current travel advisories, especially for areas near the Somali border.

name: Wajir
climate: Hot and dry, with very little rain. Days are long and sunny.
food: Camel milk, goat and camel meat, rice and Somali-style breads.
transport: Flights and long road journeys connect Wajir to Nairobi; roads within the county can be rough.
vibe: Remote pastoralist country with a strong community spirit. Check current travel advisories for border areas before visiting.

name: Mandera
knownFor: meeting point of Kenya, Ethiopia and Somalia
climate: Very hot and dry for most of the year, with short, unreliable rains.
food: Somali-style food: rice, meat, anjero and sweet spiced tea.
transport: Most visitors fly in, as the road from Nairobi is very long. Local travel is by road between towns.
vibe: A far-off border county with close ties across the borders. Check current travel advisories before planning any visit.

name: Marsabit
climate: Mostly hot and dry desert, though Marsabit mountain is cooler and often misty.
food: Simple pastoralist food such as meat, milk and maize, with tea served almost everywhere.
transport: A good tarmac road links Isiolo to Marsabit town and on to Moyale, but travel to remote areas needs a sturdy vehicle.
vibe: Vast and remote, home to several pastoralist communities. Check current travel advisories for border areas.

name: Isiolo
knownFor: Samburu and Buffalo Springs reserves (shared border)
climate: Hot and dry, with short rains around April and November.
food: Meat dishes, rice and Somali and Borana influences, plus plenty of sweet tea.
transport: Isiolo sits on the main tarmac road north from Nairobi and has an airport.
vibe: A frontier-style trading town where many northern communities meet.

name: Meru
climate: Cool and green on the mountain slopes, hotter and drier on the lower plains.
food: Plenty of fresh produce, bananas, potatoes and githeri (maize and beans).
transport: Matatus link Meru to Nairobi and nearby towns; roads to the national park are partly unpaved.
vibe: A busy farming county with a lively market town at its heart.

name: Tharaka-Nithi
climate: Cool and wet on the upper slopes, hot and dry in the lower Tharaka area.
food: Everyday Kenyan food, with millet, sorghum and fruit grown locally.
transport: The main Embu–Meru road passes through Chuka, with matatus to other towns.
vibe: Quiet, rural and agricultural, with a student buzz in Chuka.

name: Embu
climate: Mild and fairly wet in the uplands, hotter and drier lower down.
food: Fresh vegetables, bananas and maize dishes, plus roasted meat (nyama choma).
transport: Embu is on the main road around Mount Kenya, with frequent matatus to Nairobi.
vibe: A friendly, mid-sized town surrounded by green farms.

name: Kitui
climate: Hot and dry for much of the year, with two short rainy seasons.
food: Kamba favourites such as muthokoi (hulled maize and beans) and drought-tolerant crops like millet.
transport: Roads link Kitui to Nairobi via Machakos; inside the county distances are large.
vibe: Wide, rural and down-to-earth, with strong Kamba traditions.

name: Machakos
knownFor: Athi River and Mlolongo industrial areas
climate: Warm and fairly dry, with cooler hills around Machakos town.
food: Kamba dishes like muthokoi and nyama choma, plus fruit such as mangoes and oranges.
transport: Close to Nairobi, with frequent matatus and good roads. The Nairobi–Mombasa road and SGR pass through the county.
vibe: Part commuter belt, part rural hills, and growing fast.

name: Makueni
climate: Warm and dry for much of the year, cooler in the hills.
food: Fruit, especially mangoes, plus Kamba favourites such as muthokoi.
transport: The Nairobi–Mombasa road and SGR run along the county; matatus serve the main towns.
vibe: Quiet and rural, with dramatic volcanic hills in the south.

name: Nyandarua
climate: Cool, high and often chilly, especially at night. Bring a warm layer.
food: Potatoes in many forms, plus maize, cabbage, milk and mukimo (mashed potatoes, greens and maize).
transport: Matatus connect the main towns to Nakuru and Nyahururu; some rural roads are rough.
vibe: High-altitude farming country, peaceful and green.

name: Nyeri
climate: Mild to cool, with misty mornings and two rainy seasons.
food: Central Kenyan dishes like mukimo and githeri, with good local coffee.
transport: Good tarmac roads link Nyeri to Nairobi, Nanyuki and Karatina by matatu.
vibe: A tidy, green highland town and a common base for Mount Kenya climbs.

name: Kirinyaga
climate: Cool on the mountain side, warmer on the Mwea plains.
food: Pishori rice from Mwea is famous; you will also find mukimo and fresh vegetables.
transport: Matatus run to Nairobi and nearby towns on good roads.
vibe: A small, busy farming county with a practical, hardworking feel.

name: Murang'a
climate: Mild and fairly wet, cooler in the western highlands.
food: Fresh avocados, bananas and Central Kenyan staples like mukimo and githeri.
transport: The Nairobi–Nyeri road passes nearby; matatus serve most towns.
vibe: Rolling green hills and farms, with a strong sense of Kikuyu heritage.

name: Kiambu
climate: Mild and pleasant, with cool evenings and two rainy seasons.
food: Everything from roadside roasted maize to city-style restaurants, with plenty of tea grown locally.
transport: Very well connected to Nairobi by matatu, the Thika Superhighway and commuter rail.
vibe: Part busy commuter suburbs, part quiet tea country.

name: Turkana
knownFor: Nariokotome, where the Turkana Boy fossil was found
climate: Very hot and dry desert climate, with strong winds near the lake.
food: Fish from the lake, goat meat and milk, with simple local meals in town.
transport: Flights connect Lodwar to Nairobi; road travel is long and needs planning.
vibe: Vast, remote and striking, with strong pastoralist traditions. Check current travel advisories for border areas.

name: West Pokot
climate: Cool in the highlands, hot and dry in the lowlands.
food: Maize, milk, meat and local vegetables.
transport: Road access from Kitale is good to Kapenguria, but rougher further in.
vibe: Scenic, rural and traditional. Check local advice before travelling in remote lowland areas.

name: Samburu
climate: Hot and dry in the lowlands, cooler around Maralal.
food: Meat and milk-based pastoralist food, with simple Kenyan staples in towns.
transport: Most safari visitors come by road via Isiolo or by charter flight; local roads are rough.
vibe: Wide, wild country with colourful local traditions.

name: Trans Nzoia
climate: Mild and fairly wet, ideal for farming.
food: Plenty of maize, so ugali is everywhere, plus beans, milk and fresh vegetables.
transport: Matatus link Kitale to Eldoret and Western Kenya; Kitale also has a small airstrip.
vibe: Calm farming country with a busy market town.

name: Uasin Gishu
climate: Cool highland weather, with chilly mornings and rain in the middle of the year.
food: Kalenjin favourites like mursik (fermented milk) and ugali, plus city restaurants.
transport: Eldoret has an international airport and good roads to Nairobi, Kisumu and Uganda.
vibe: A fast-growing city with a sporting, can-do spirit.

name: Elgeyo-Marakwet
climate: Cool on the high escarpment, hot down in the Kerio Valley.
food: Simple Kalenjin food such as ugali, greens and mursik.
transport: Matatus connect Iten to Eldoret; roads into the valley are steep and winding.
vibe: Dramatic scenery and early-morning runners everywhere.

name: Nandi
climate: Cool and wet, which suits the tea gardens.
food: Kalenjin staples like ugali and mursik, with plenty of tea.
transport: Matatus connect the towns to Eldoret and Kisumu.
vibe: Rolling green tea country, peaceful and proud of its sporting heroes.

name: Baringo
knownFor: flamingos and hot springs at Bogoria
climate: Hot and dry around the lakes, cooler up in the Tugen Hills around Kabarnet.
food: Fish from Lake Baringo, goat meat and local staples.
transport: Good tarmac road from Nakuru to Marigat and Kabarnet; remote areas need care.
vibe: Scenic lakes and hills. Check local advice before travelling in remote northern parts.

name: Laikipia
climate: Cool and dry on a high plateau, with sunny days and cold nights.
food: Mix of local food and international cafés in Nanyuki.
transport: Nanyuki has an airstrip and good roads to Nairobi. Conservancies are reached by road or charter flight.
vibe: Wide open ranches and wildlife, with Nanyuki as the lively hub.
verify: verify areaKm2 against KNBS; Nyahururu straddles the Laikipia/Nyandarua border

name: Nakuru
climate: Mild and pleasant most of the year, with occasional dusty dry spells.
food: Wide choice in Nakuru city, fish from Lake Naivasha and good roadside nyama choma.
transport: Major highways and frequent matatus link Nakuru and Naivasha to Nairobi.
vibe: A growing city with lakes, parks and flower farms nearby.

name: Narok
knownFor: the Great Migration (roughly July to October)
climate: Mild and fairly dry, with cool nights in the Mara.
food: Safari lodge meals for most visitors, plus nyama choma and local food in Narok town.
transport: Most visitors go by road from Nairobi or fly into Mara airstrips.
vibe: World-famous safari country with strong Maasai traditions.

name: Kajiado
knownFor: Amboseli National Park and views of Kilimanjaro
climate: Warm and dry, with cooler hills near Ngong.
food: Nyama choma is popular, especially in Kitengela, plus Maasai milk-based foods.
transport: Close to Nairobi; matatus serve the suburbs, while Amboseli is reached by road or air.
vibe: A mix of fast-growing Nairobi suburbs and open Maasai rangeland.

name: Kericho
climate: Cool with frequent afternoon rain, which is great for tea.
food: Local Kalenjin dishes and, of course, lots of very fresh tea.
transport: On the main road between Nakuru and Kisumu, with frequent matatus.
vibe: Calm, green and orderly, surrounded by neat tea gardens.

name: Bomet
climate: Mild and fairly wet in the hills.
food: Kalenjin food like ugali, greens and mursik, with fresh milk.
transport: Matatus connect Bomet to Kericho, Narok and Kisii.
vibe: Quiet farming county with friendly small towns.

name: Kakamega
climate: Warm and wet, with rain on many afternoons.
food: Luhya favourites like ingokho (chicken), ugali and traditional vegetables.
transport: Good roads to Kisumu and Eldoret; matatus and boda bodas are everywhere.
vibe: Lively, green and welcoming, with lots of music and culture.

name: Vihiga
knownFor: one of Kenya's smallest and most densely populated counties
climate: Warm and wet, with green hills all year.
food: Luhya dishes, ugali, chicken and traditional vegetables like kunde and mrenda.
transport: On the main Kisumu–Kakamega road, served by matatus and boda bodas.
vibe: Busy, close-knit and very rural despite its high population.

name: Bungoma
climate: Warm and wet in the lowlands, cool on Mount Elgon.
food: Luhya favourites such as ugali, chicken and local greens.
transport: On the main road and railway to Uganda via Malaba; matatus serve all towns.
vibe: A busy agricultural county with deep cultural traditions.

name: Busia
knownFor: Lake Victoria shore at Port Victoria
climate: Warm and humid, with plenty of rain.
food: Fish from Lake Victoria, ugali and cassava dishes.
transport: Busy border town on the main road to Uganda; boda bodas are common.
vibe: Bustling border trade mixed with quiet lakeside villages.

name: Siaya
climate: Warm and fairly humid, with two rainy seasons.
food: Fresh tilapia and omena (small fish) with ugali.
transport: Roads link Siaya to Kisumu; boda bodas and matatus serve the villages.
vibe: Calm rural lakeside life.

name: Kisumu
climate: Hot and humid, with afternoon thunderstorms in the rainy seasons.
food: Fried or grilled tilapia with ugali by the lake is a must.
transport: Kisumu has an international airport and good roads; tuk-tuks and boda bodas get you around.
vibe: A warm, relaxed lakeside city with great music and nightlife.

name: Homa Bay
climate: Warm and fairly dry for the lake region, with two rainy seasons.
food: Fresh lake fish, omena and ugali.
transport: Road links to Kisumu and Kisii; boats serve the islands.
vibe: Scenic lakeside county with quiet islands and fishing villages.

name: Migori
climate: Warm with plenty of rain.
food: Fish, ugali and local vegetables.
transport: On the main road to Tanzania; matatus and boda bodas are common.
vibe: A busy trading area close to the Tanzanian border.

name: Kisii
climate: Cool, wet and green, with rain on many afternoons.
food: Bananas cooked many ways (matoke), ugali and traditional greens.
transport: Good roads to Kisumu and Kericho; matatus and boda bodas are everywhere.
vibe: A busy, crowded and friendly highland town.

name: Nyamira
climate: Cool and wet for much of the year.
food: Bananas, ugali and local greens, with plenty of tea.
transport: Matatus connect Nyamira to Kisii and Kericho.
vibe: Quiet, green tea country.

name: Nairobi City
knownFor: Giraffe Centre and Sheldrick elephant orphanage
climate: Mild most of the year thanks to the altitude, with cool mornings. Long rains usually fall from about March to May.
food: Everything from nyama choma and chapati to international restaurants, plus street food like smokie pasua.
transport: Matatus, buses, boda bodas and ride-hailing apps; traffic can be heavy at rush hour. JKIA is the main international airport.
vibe: Energetic, ambitious and always busy, with green leafy suburbs and a buzzing centre.
